1.why: Text uses a clean, legible sans-serif with comfortable line height and spaced monospace for codes, though letter spacing in prose is default rather than notably generous.

2.why: All instructional prose is short, sentence-case, and free of italics, with uppercase limited to the code values themselves and no dense paragraphs.

3.why: The narrow single-column card layout with full-width inputs, large buttons, and wrapping text should reflow well at phone width, although only desktop-width screenshots were provided.

4.why: Every screen's guidance is a single short plain-language sentence, e.g. 'Create a test-only secret, then add it manually to your authenticator app.'

5.why: The mobile number field shows a format placeholder (+44 7700 900000) and the demo credentials line illustrates login input, but the recovery-code box never shows an example format when empty.

6.why: No step requires reading a long block of text; all prompts are one-line sentences plus short code lists, and the log panel is optional test-only output.

7.why: The setup secret and recovery codes are rendered as selectable plain text (not images) so they can be copied, but no copy-to-clipboard button is provided and the wording directs manual entry.

8.why: The flow explicitly says to 'add it manually to your authenticator app' and no QR code or equivalent alternative appears on any screen.

9.why: The login uses conventional email/password inputs that password managers typically handle, but nothing visible (autocomplete hints, OTP autofill support) confirms or refutes autofill support.

10.why: The primary blue action button is visually dominant on every screen, but the breadcrumb trail renders all four steps identically with no highlight of the current step.

11.why: Each enrolment screen asks for a single primary action (Sign in, Continue, Create secret, I saved these codes), though the settings hub presents three buttons at once.

12.why: Status banners plainly state outcomes and next steps ('MFA is enabled. Save these one-time codes now.', 'Recovery code accepted.'), but some transitions such as after sign-in give no explicit statement of what just happened.

13.why: Back buttons and 'Please try again' allow retrying, and 'Generate new recovery codes' re-issues codes with no lockout or penalty observed, although the password field lacks a reveal/hide toggle.

14.why: The only error shown ('We could not complete that request. Please try again.') is non-blaming but vague, neither identifying the actual problem nor giving a specific fix.

15.why: No countdown, expiry indicator, or session timeout appears on any step, including the code-entry screens, so reading and entry are untimed.
